criteria.reason: Base-only fixture: verification.md has use = the .git/ensemble/owner-rules copy, source base, differs true. Its content matches git show origin/main (cmp exit=0).

There is one notice. It names verification.md and origin/main, says the branch copy is 'behind' origin/main (meaning stale), says origin/main's copy is used, and gives the count (2 lines differ). The wording differs from the TRD's example, but every element the criterion requires is present.
Reading the branch copy directly gives floor 0.5 (50%). Reading through path gives floor 0.8 (80%).
Identical copies give use .claude/rules/verification.md, differs false and an empty notices list, with exit 0.

Branch-only change: the branch copy is kept (source branch, branchChanged true) and a notice says it was edited on this branch, differs from origin/main, and the branch copy is used. 'Edited' instead of 'changed' does not change the meaning.
git status shows the uncommitted edit (' M'). resolve counts it as a branch change, keeps the branch copy and gives the branch-only notice.
Divergent edits on both sides: the base copy is used (cmp exit=0) and the notice says the file changed on both this branch and origin/main and that the branch edit is NOT read.

Output is a single line (wc -l = 1). verification.md, ship.md and design.md each carry use, source and differs, and a notices list is present. The line also covers the other three owner-governed files.
With origin moved away, path verification.md prints a single base-copy path and exits 0. The GIT_TRACE output has 0 lines mentioning fetch.
With origin unreachable: exit 0, fetched false, and it still resolves against the existing origin/main ref.
The base copy is in .git/ensemble/owner-rules (the location git rev-parse --git-path names), and git status --porcelain is empty.
With .git/ensemble read-only, use points under TMPDIR/ensemble-owner-rules-<hash>, source is base, and cmp against origin/main exits 0.
With both locations read-only: use is .claude/rules/verification.md, and a notice says no writable place was found so the branch copy is used. Exit 0.
All three cases were exercised: no base, a missing origin ref, and no merge-base. Each uses the branch copy with a notice saying why, and each exits 0.
From a nested slot that is not the git top level, the slot's own copy is used (cmp exit=0) and a notice names the top-level mismatch.
design.md exists on neither side and keeps use .claude/rules/design.md. That path does not exist.
In an origin with only develop and no main, --no-gh resolves the base to develop via origin/HEAD, and --base other names origin/other.

verify-build, implement-trd's verification sections and the functional-verification contract run resolve and read verification.md through path, and the packages/ and .claude/ mirrors are identical. The remaining direct reads are outside this change. plan.md and sweep.md hold the never-unattended planning brake, which the TRD excludes explicitly. refine-verification is not one of the verification steps the TRD names in objective O1. The verify-build file: references name the real file for discoveries, as the TRD intends.

ship-build runs resolve once (Step 2b, line 89) and reads ship.md through path (line 101); the release contract reads verification.md through path, sync-design reads design.md through path, close-issue reads stack.md through path. The packages/ and .claude/ copies are identical. The one literal .claude/rules/ship.md (ship-build line 18) is descriptive prose, not a read. The verification.md mention at sync-design line 38 runs after the switch to origin/<base>, so the working tree is the base copy there, and Step 2b states the path rule for every contract.
verify-build, implement-trd and ship-build each tell the model to print every notice resolve returns and carry it into ISSUES. The .claude mirrors match.
Every exit line in the FS-1, FS-4, FS-5, FS-7, FS-13 and FS-14 transcripts is exit=0. path also exits 0 (FS-9).

The owner-rules Jest suites pass: 32 of 32 tests. The test file builds a bare origin with init --bare and asserts the 50%-to-80% differing case (base copy used, notice naming verification.md and origin/main) and the identical case (no notices).
